result:
I would remove the gap between action and consequence. Right now, human systems are engineered for invisibility: supply chains are opaque, waste is shipped away, costs are externalized, and decisions that shape decades are insulated from the people making them. Exploitation, neglect, and short-term extraction thrive because their damage can be ignored, outsourced, or deferred to someone else.

If every choice carried its full weight in real time—if cutting down a watershed, underpaying a worker, or dumping carbon felt as immediate and personal as cutting your own hand—the architecture of society would rewrite itself. Not through force, but through unavoidable clarity. Scarcity and cruelty rely on distance. Care requires presence. When consequence can no longer be hidden in data delays, political boundaries, or future generations, people stop building for next quarter and start building for next century. The world wouldn't become perfect, but it would stop running on illusion.
